caveats: The existing 6 GiB parent cap differs from the official 16 GiB VM; load generation is outside the target unit but shares the container/host.
Whole-server samples are one fixed-order pass; storage/cache variation prevents attributing tail differences to language or allocator.
All 32-writer profiles have zero errors, but both private-Nelibc cases miss at least one latency threshold in the normal run.
The later private-Nelibc quota-pulse recovery run passes, showing substantial run-to-run tail variation; it is not capacity/ranking evidence.
Per-PID sampled PG CPU can miss exited workers; target cgroup CPU and memory avoid counting PG shared RSS repeatedly.
